section_summary: Pages 1-80 cover Nov-Dec 1949 State Department Division of Protective Services (DS) handling of civilian and commercial entry into occupied Japan. They mainly consist of Army Pacific Military Permit Branch action slips, outgoing telegrams and letters forwarding applications and permits (Kraslavsky, Vilimovitch, Shvetz, Nahmias, Seto, Feldman, Aldridge, Kaptzan and others). The section also holds a Department/SCAP exchange on SCAPIN 2035 about travel abroad of Japanese technicians. Foreign-post queries about procedure for alien applicants (Brazil, Belgian Congo) and the Wiebke transit case are also included.

subfiles.about: Covering letter on policy toward Japanese technician travel and Point Four, enclosing a memorandum.

subfiles.about: States US policy that technician travel should be treated as normal and encouraged.

subfiles.about: Comments on SCAPIN 2035 and the policy of travel abroad of Japanese technicians.
subfiles.summary: Says SCAPIN 2035 treats technician travel as exceptional and involves SCAP unnecessarily. Objects to four provisions: limits on competing industries, work only on Japanese equipment, hard-currency payment, welfare conditions, and destination-government endorsement. Suggests normal visa procedures.
subfiles.title: Letter to West on SCAPIN 2035

subfiles.about: Copy of SCAP memorandum liberalizing technician travel abroad.

subfiles.about: SCAP instruction liberalizing travel abroad of Japanese technicians.
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy for Supreme Commander
subfiles.summary: Defines technicians, requires government endorsement, contract basis, payment partly in acceptable currency into SCAP commercial accounts, no dependents, no numerical limit. Japanese agency to coordinate with Economic and Scientific Section.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2035: Travel of Japanese Technicians Outside of Japan
